Extract Neighborhoods from an Edge List

Source: R/extract_neighborhoods.R
extract_neighborhoods.Rd

For each cell in the edge list, identifies its spatial neighbors and the edges that fall within its neighborhood. Returns three structures suitable for populating the neighborhood slots of a NICHESObject.

Usage

extract_neighborhoods(
  edge.list,
  edge.filter.mode = "both_in_neighborhood",
  remove.autocrine = FALSE,
  n.cores = 1,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

edge.list

A data.table with columns edge, SendingCell, and ReceivingCell. Typically niches.obj$edge.list or output of create_Edgelist_Spatial().

edge.filter.mode

Character. One of:

"both_in_neighborhood"

(default) Both endpoints of an edge must be in the cell's neighborhood (cell itself + its neighbors).

"any_in_neighborhood"

At least one endpoint must be in the neighborhood.

"central_cell_only"

The central cell must be an endpoint.

remove.autocrine

Logical. If TRUE, removes self-loops from the adjacency (neighbor) list. Autocrine edges may still appear in neighborhood.edge.list if they pass the edge filter. Default FALSE.

n.cores

Integer. Number of cores for parallel processing. Default 1 (serial).

verbose

Logical. Print progress messages. Default TRUE.

Value

A list with three elements:

neighborhood.cell.list

Named list of character vectors. Each element is keyed by a cell barcode and contains the barcodes of its neighbors.

neighborhood.edge.list

Named list of character vectors. Each element is keyed by a cell barcode and contains the edge IDs (format "SendingCell|ReceivingCell") belonging to that cell's neighborhood.

neighborhood.meta

A data.table with columns cell, n.neighbors, n.edges, keyed on cell.

Attributes: "edge.filter.mode", "remove.autocrine".

Details

Neighborhoods are defined topologically from the edge list: cell B is a neighbor of cell A if any edge connects them (in either direction). The edge.filter.mode parameter controls which edges are assigned to each cell's neighborhood.

This function is a low-level primitive: it operates on a raw edge list (a data.table of (edge, SendingCell, ReceivingCell) rows) rather than on a full NICHESObject. Most users should call add_neighborhoods instead, which extracts neighborhoods from niches.obj$edge.list and writes them back into the three neighborhood slots in one step. extract_neighborhoods() is exposed for power users and for testing pipelines that build edge lists outside the standard create_NICHESObject() workflow.

Examples

data(NICHESv2_example)
nbhd <- extract_neighborhoods(NICHESv2_example$edge.list, verbose = FALSE)
head(nbhd$neighborhood.meta)
#> Key: <cell>
#>       cell n.neighbors n.edges
#>     <char>       <int>   <int>
#> 1:  Cell_1           5      17
#> 2: Cell_10           6      30
#> 3: Cell_11           6      28
#> 4: Cell_12           4      10
#> 5: Cell_13           2       4
#> 6: Cell_14           6      30
